Draws of a covariate's future, from its own model

Source: R/ilm_covariate_paths.R, R/zzz-iml-aliases.R
ilm_covariate_paths.Rd

When a covariate is not known in advance, its uncertainty belongs in the forecast. ilm_covariate_paths() simulates future paths of the covariate from an illume model of it, and returns newdata stacked into one block of rows per path, marked by a .draw column. ilm_forecast() and ilm_predict() then mix over the paths; see Covariates given as draws in ilm_predict().

Usage

ilm_covariate_paths(
  fit,
  newdata,
  nsim = 1000L,
  uncertainty = c("joint", "fixed", "latent", "none"),
  seed = 1L
)

Arguments

fit

A fitted "ilm_model" of the covariate. Its response names the column of newdata to draw. Or a list of such fits, one per covariate.

newdata

The rows to forecast, as for ilm_forecast(), with the columns the covariate models need. The drawn columns may be missing, as ilm_future() leaves them.

nsim

The number of paths.

uncertainty

How the covariate model's own parameters enter: "joint" (the default), "fixed", "latent" or "none", as in ilm_predict().

seed

Seed for the draws. The caller's random-number state is restored afterwards.

Value

newdata repeated once per path, with a .draw column (1 to nsim) and the drawn columns filled in.

How the paths are drawn

Each path is one draw from the covariate model's predictive distribution of a new observation. That draw has three parts:

  • a draw of the model's parameters, under uncertainty;

  • each series' latent path continued over the new times, from its fitted state (groups = "fitted");

  • a new observation at each time.

So a path is joint over its times. Together, the paths carry both the covariate's future shocks and the uncertainty in its model's parameters. Give nsim the same value as the forecast's own nsim: parameter draw s of the forecast is then paired with path s.

Several covariates

Give a list of fits, one per covariate. Each covariate is drawn from its own model, independently of the others. Covariates that move together would need a joint model of them, which is not in limn yet.

See also

ilm_as_draws() for paths simulated by another tool; ilm_future() for the rows.

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(id = factor(rep(c("a", "b"), each = 30)), t = rep(1:30, 2))
d$x <- ave(rnorm(60), d$id, FUN = function(e) stats::filter(e, 0.8, "recursive"))
d$y <- 2 + 0.5 * d$x + rnorm(60, 0, 0.3)
fx <- illume::ilm_model(x ~ 1, data = d, family = "gaussian",
                        ar = illume::ilm_ar1(~ t | id), verbose = FALSE)
#> ilm_model(): the residual SD has run to zero: the model's other terms leave no residual variation, usually because a correlation over time or a random effect has about one observation per cell or level and has taken up the noise. The fixed effects and their standard errors are usable; sigma's own estimate is where the optimiser stopped, and is held there.
fy <- illume::ilm_model(y ~ x, data = d, family = "gaussian", verbose = FALSE)
fut <- ilm_future(d, time = "t", group = "id", h = 3, response = "y")
#> These columns vary over time, so their future values are not known: x. They are left missing: fill them in with the values the forecast should assume.
paths <- ilm_covariate_paths(fx, fut, nsim = 200)
head(paths)
#>   .draw id  t           x  y horizon
#> 1     1  a 31 -0.09111298 NA       1
#> 2     1  a 32  0.22876617 NA       2
#> 3     1  a 33 -0.34276990 NA       3
#> 4     1  b 31  1.48188793 NA       1
#> 5     1  b 32  0.47211188 NA       2
#> 6     1  b 33  0.42517634 NA       3
fc <- ilm_forecast(fy, paths, nsim = 200)
as.data.frame(fc)
#>   id  t  x  y horizon new_level estimate     mean lower_0.9 upper_0.9
#> 1  a 31 NA NA       1     FALSE 1.901752 1.899944  1.082757  2.698562
#> 2  a 32 NA NA       2     FALSE 2.022371 2.018640  1.112669  2.921620
#> 3  a 33 NA NA       3     FALSE 2.119380 2.101238  1.087254  3.050851
#> 4  b 31 NA NA       1     FALSE 2.338161 2.353596  1.539417  3.232534
#> 5  b 32 NA NA       2     FALSE 2.276033 2.281953  1.433222  3.161757
#> 6  b 33 NA NA       3     FALSE 2.292942 2.298043  1.364966  3.252102
